tagline: Founders and the people who fund them
sector: A paid two-day founders summit in Portland, Oregon, for founders, operators and institutional investors.
founded_place_size: Founded 2024, Portland, Oregon, now in its second edition, run by a core team of four staff for a room of about four hundred.
about: Cascadia Founders Summit is a two-day gathering for founders and the people who back them. Passes run six hundred to twelve hundred dollars and the room is roughly four hundred people who read the calibre of the event off its details. The summit sells seriousness and access rather than spectacle, and everything it puts in front of that audience is meant to look considered.
audience: Founders, operators and institutional investors aged 28 to 55 who expense the ticket and judge the event by how professional it feels.
price_positioning: Delegate passes 600 to 1,200 dollars, a credible professional summit priced above a free meetup and below a flagship conference. Restraint reads as calibre; a glossy or busy treatment would misprice it.
typography: A restrained contemporary serif for titles paired with a clean neutral sans for names, role lines and body copy. Even and quiet, with no display flourish.
voice: Plain, direct and professional, confident without selling hard. Example line: Passes are limited and the room is small on purpose.
brand_assets_status: The summit builds its own website and needs no pages. Its badge artwork exists only as the press PDF the venue printer ran last year, with no working file behind it. The house ground, mark and tone are described in the brand notes rather than handed over as a kit.
values: A serious room worth the price of admission, where credibility is read off the smallest details.
